vocabulary.meaning: watching or listening to media over the internet without downloading the whole file first
examples: Streaming has changed how people watch television.
Music streaming is now common around the world.

vocabulary.meaning: an arrangement in which you pay regularly for access to a service
examples: We cancelled one streaming subscription.
Many households pay for several subscriptions.

vocabulary.meaning: available whenever a user chooses rather than at a fixed broadcast time
examples: Viewers prefer on-demand programmes.
The service offers films on demand.

vocabulary.meaning: an online service that provides digital content or interaction
examples: Several streaming platforms compete for viewers.
The series is available on only one platform.

vocabulary.meaning: to watch many episodes of a programme one after another
examples: We binge-watched the series over the weekend.
Streaming services make it easy to binge-watch.

vocabulary.meaning: films, programmes, music, articles, or other material provided to users
examples: The platform invests heavily in original content.
Users can choose from a huge amount of content.

vocabulary.meaning: to transmit a programme by television, radio, or another system
examples: Traditional broadcasters now also use streaming.
The match will be broadcast live.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who watches television or online video
examples: Streaming gives viewers more control.
Younger viewers often watch less traditional television.

vocabulary.meaning: a set of computer rules used to make decisions or recommendations
examples: The platform's algorithm recommends programmes based on viewing history.
Algorithms influence what content users discover.

vocabulary.meaning: the practice of cancelling traditional cable or satellite television in favour of online services
examples: Cord-cutting has increased as streaming services have grown.
Some families save money by cord-cutting.
